title: Model onboarding observability checklist & walkthrough
content:
Purpose:
This is a lean, operator-friendly playbook for onboarding a new model (open or imported) into Redwood’s inference stack. Focus: minimal metric set + trace contracts + one-page dashboard wireframe + 72h verification checklist.

Audience:
- Applied ML engineer integrating a model
- Observability engineer reviewing instrumentation
- SRE/Support doing first-72h ops for a new model rollout

Why this file exists (context):
- We often ship models with lots of scattered telemetry; teams get overloaded. This file prescribes the minimal signal set and a short verification flow to get useful visibility fast.
- Designed to be copied into a model-specific onboarding doc and extended as needed.

Minimal metric contract (must-have names + semantics) — keep names short, stable, and tagged by model/version:
1) inference.request.count: counter per model, per route, tag: outcome={ok,error,timeout,rate_limited}  — incremented at request start.
2) inference.request.latency_ms: histogram (p50,p90,p99) measured at end of response (wall-clock). tag: stage={frontend,router,executor}  — helps separate network vs execution latency.
3) inference.token.generated.count: counter per model + tenant — counts tokens emitted (useful for cost and batching).
4) inference.kvcache.hit_rate: gauge or derived ratio taggable by model/tenant — measured at executor when reading KV-cache for next token.
5) inference.memory.gpu_percent: gauge per GPU host and model allocation — rough memory pressure.
6) inference.model.load.duration_ms: histogram when loading model artifact into pool (cold-start).
7) inference.batch.size: histogram of batch sizes at inference execution (helps tuning batching).
8) inference.error.type: counter with error_type tag (oom,invalid_input,model_crash,timeout) — use sparse taxonomy.
9) inference.cost.estimated_token_usd: gauge derived from tokens * pricing profile (optional but useful for early experiments).

Metric tagging guidance (brief):
- Required tags: model_name, model_version, tenant_id (if applicable), region, deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Optional: routing_policy, quantization_profile, seq_length_bucket (short/medium/long).
- Keep tag cardinality low: tenant_id only for high-volume tenants; otherwise use tenant_cohort (free/paid/enterprise).

Trace span model (minimal):
- Root span: trace.request (attributes: request_id, model_name, model_version, route).
- Child spans (ordered):
  * span: router.lookup (attributes: routing_policy, route_id) — fast lookup for routing decisions.
  * span: prefix.cache (attributes: cache_hit=true|false, cache_key) — short-lived; sample all misses.
  * span: kvcache.read (attributes: kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_latency_ms) — keep kv_hits numeric.
  * span: batch.assemble (attributes: batch_size, tenant_cohort) — shows batching grouping time.
  * span: executor.execute (attributes: perf_kernel, seq_length, quant_profile) — heavy span, sample at 100% for p99 investigation windows.
  * span: model.step/token_emit (attributes: tokens_emitted, token_latency_ms) — optional, only for heavy debugging.
  * span: response.serialize (attributes: payload_bytes, compression)
- Sampling policy: sample 1% broadly, 100% for error outcomes, 100% for cold-start load spans and prefix.cache misses.
- PII/PHI redaction: never record full prompt/user content. Record prompt length and a checksum-only fingerprint (sha256-prefix) if needed for replay linking — document local privacy policy in model-specific onboarding.

Dashboard wireframe (one page, single-pane checklist):
- Top row (SLO + quick facts): model_name/version, current requests/min, rolling error rate (5m), p90 latency, median token rate, KV cache hit rate, active GPUs.
- Middle: latency heatmap (time vs seq_length_bucket) + request rate timeseries annotated with deployment events (deploy, scale).
- Left column: small panels: batch size distribution (p50/p90), cold-starts (count last 24h), current inflight requests.
- Right column: top errors (error_type), recent traces sample links (5 recent error traces), top tenants by error rate.
- Bottom: cost estimate panel (tokens * price) + predicted saturation (based on batch size trends).
- Drill links: each panel must link to a saved trace query and to the model-specific runbook page.

72-hour verification checklist (practical):
Pre-launch (0):
- [ ] Add metric names and tags to model integration PR.
- [ ] Confirm agent-level tracing is enabled and root span attributes are present.
- [ ] Add saved dashboard (template copy) and set dashboard owner.
Launch day (0-6h):
- [ ] Verify request.count and latency_ms emitting for first requests.
- [ ] Check p50/p90 latency roughly within expected envelope. If p99 > target, stop rollout and investigate.
- [ ] Confirm no high-cardinality tag explosion (monitor unique tenant_id tag count).
- [ ] Sample traces for 10 requests and confirm spans present and attributes match contract.
First day (24h):
- [ ] Observe KV cache hit_rate trend; expect ramping up after warmup window. 
- [ ] Confirm batch.size distribution sensical (matches traffic pattern).
- [ ] Verify no OOMs in executor logs; if OOMs, capture trace+metrics and reduce batch or quantize.
First 72h:
- [ ] Look at error.type top contributors; create quick mitigations (retry policy, fallback model).
- [ ] Validate telemetry costs (query cost + storage) against budget; reduce retention for high-volume debug traces.
- [ ] Confirm runbook entries for 2 common incidents (high-latency by seq length, prefix cache cold miss).

Troubleshooting quick recipes (copy-paste commands/snippets):
- Find recent cold-starts: metrics filter: metric = inference.model.load.duration_ms > 1000 AND model_name=XYZ => link to traces where model.load occurred.
- Inspect high-p99 latency: filter traces where inference.request.latency_ms > threshold and sample 100% of those traces.
- KV cache investigation: correlate kvcache.read latency with prefix.cache misses; pivot on session_id.

Open questions / decisions to make during onboarding (to resolve with product/ML):
- Do we persist prompt fingerprints for debugging across private deployments (consent + retention)?
- Default sampling rates for low-traffic models — should we increase to 5% for early trials?
- Tagging policy for tenant_id: when does it become a required tag vs tenant_cohort?

Notes to self (rough):
- Try to enforce metric naming via a linter in the model integration PR template.
- Push a dashboard template into the onboarding repo so teams can auto-create a copy.
- Consider a compact trace view: only show router.lookup, kvcache.read, executor.execute for the default trace UI to reduce noise.

Appendix: example tracing attributes (CSV-like list):
attribute_name,example_values,description
request_id,abcd-1234,unique per request
model_name,gpt-13b,model id
model_version,v0.3.1,semantic version
route_id,chat-default,routing label
routing_policy,cold-start-prefer-small,policy string
cache_hit,true|false,boolean
kv_hits,2,integer count
batch_size,1-64,integer
perf_kernel,flash_attn_v2,executor kernel choice
seq_length,34,sequence length
error_type,oom,tokenizer_error,short taxonomy

End — copy this file into the model repo (docs/observability.md) and fill any model-specific policy decisions.

Quick contact: Asha (asham@redwood.ai) — ping on #observability if you need help wiring the first traces.
